posts.text:
How much does a missed call cost you?

A quick way to check, with your own numbers:
1. Count the calls that went to voicemail last week.
2. Estimate how many were new customers.
3. Multiply by the value of a first order or appointment.

Example with illustrative figures: 15 missed calls a week, one in five a new customer worth £150. That is about £1,900 a month walking to a competitor.

An AI receptionist answers those calls, books them into your calendar and sends you a summary. Full cost breakdown: {link}

posts.text:
“Press 1 for bookings, press 2 for…” Most callers hang up before option 4.

An AI voice agent works differently. The caller says what they need in their own words, and the agent books, answers or passes the call to a person.

What it should never do on its own: give clinical, legal or financial advice, quote prices outside your rules, or keep an upset caller on the line.

Consultants make every shortlist and every decision. Under UK GDPR, that is also the safe way to design it.

posts.text:
“Where do we even start with AI?”

A plan that works for most businesses:
• Weeks 1–2: audit one workflow and agree one metric
• Weeks 3–6: pilot on real data, with a person approving
• Weeks 7–10: roll out to the team and write the rules
• Weeks 11–13: start the second workflow, reusing what you built

posts.text:
A support chatbot is only as good as what it reads.

Before the bot, build the knowledge base:
• start from questions customers actually ask, not from your brochure
• one approved answer per topic, with an owner and a review date
• prices and policies from the live source, not a copy
• a clear rule for what goes to a person
